Plot the results of a calibration check

Source: R/fp_calibrate.R
plot.fp_calibration.Rd

Plots the coverage (or bias) of one scored quantity against the column of the design that varies, one colour per model. Coverage is shown with an interval of two Monte Carlo standard errors and a dashed line at the nominal level; bias, with a dashed line at zero.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_calibration'
plot(
  x,
  parameter = "occ_x",
  type = c("coverage", "bias"),
  by = NULL,
  verified = c("fraction", "sites", "occasions"),
  target = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An fp_calibration object from fp_calibrate() or fp_verification_curve().

parameter

Scored quantity to plot, by default the occupancy slope ("occ_x"). See fp_calibrate() for the others.

type

"coverage" (default) or "bias".

by

Name of the design column for the horizontal axis. By default, the first design column that varies among cells; further varying columns become panels. With no varying column, the models are on the axis.

verified

How to show the verification effort when by is "frac_verified": as the fraction of sites (default), as the expected number of verified sites ("sites", frac_verified * nsite), or as the expected number of verified occasions, e.g. clips listened to ("occasions", times nver), which is closer to the cost of the design.

target

Optional coverage to mark with a second line, for instance the lowest coverage you are willing to accept (0.90).

...

Unused.

Value

A 'ggplot2' object, which can be modified with the usual + syntax.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cal <- fp_verification_curve(p10 = 0.05, conf_effect = 1.5, conf_cor = 0.7,
                             models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),
                             reps = 50)
plot(cal)
plot(cal, type = "bias")
} # }
